summary: This regulation requires companies with listed non-convertible securities to prepare, submit, and publish their financial results within set timelines. They must share these results with stock exchanges, have them approved and signed properly, and include specific financial ratios and details. Companies must also report how they use the money raised from issuing these securities.
points: Prepare and submit un-audited or audited quarterly financial results within forty-five days from the end of the quarter, except for the last quarter.
Submit the financial results for the last quarter of the financial year within sixty days from the end of the quarter.
Provide a copy of the financial results to Debenture Trustees on the same day if debt securities are listed.
Ensure un-audited quarterly results are accompanied by a limited review report prepared by statutory auditors.
Have the submitted quarterly financial results approved by the board of directors and signed by an authorized person.
Publish the financial results and required line items in at least one English national daily newspaper within two working days of the board meeting.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited has listed its non-convertible securities on a recognized stock exchange. For the first quarter, the company prepares its un-audited standalone financial results and ensures they are accompanied by a limited review report from its statutory auditors. The board of directors approves these results, and the managing director signs them. Within forty-five days from the end of the quarter, Meera Textiles submits the financial results to the recognized stock exchange. Because the company has listed debt securities, it also provides a copy of these financial results to the Debenture Trustees on the very same day.

terms.meaning: Financial results covering the company alone, without combining its subsidiaries.
Official accountants appointed to audit a company's financial records.
Persons or entities appointed to protect the interests of holders of debt securities.

watch: People often confuse quarterly deadlines with annual deadlines or mix up the rules for the last quarter of the financial year.
